summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timeline. Customer evaluating hosted for speed to market, dedicated for predictable throughput/cost, and private for compliance. Agreed next steps: benchmark run, pricing, and security docs.
topics: Workload sizing (TPS, tokens per request, concurrency)
Benchmark plan and metrics (p50/p95, cold start, e2e)
Deployment decision criteria: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Security and compliance: SOC2/ISO, KMS, VPC
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-05-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan, Samir, Ava (Redwood); Laura, Miguel, Priya, Tom (Zenith)
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda: align success criteria, sizing, and pick a deployment path for the POC - hosted, dedicated or private.

00:18 Laura: Thanks, Jordan. Quick context, we're a retail SaaS, doing personalized product recs and search. We want something in prod by Q3 and need to make a go/no-go decision on deployment model by end of May.

00:35 Miguel: Right, our goals are: sub-200ms p95 latency for online recs, throughput ~250 reqs/s during peak, and cost per 1M tokens < $X — still working that number internally — and of course data controls for PII.
00:52 Samir: Got it. For clarity, when you say 250 reqs/s is that concurrent requests or sustained TPS?
01:02 Miguel: That's sustained peak TPS with bursts up to 400 for black-friday style events for short windows.

01:18 Jordan: Cool. High level: hosted is fastest to spin up and we can run benchmarks on Redwood hosted right away; dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable latency and cost; private (VPC/on-prem) covers strict compliance but has longer lead time and more ops involvement.
01:36 Priya: From security, our must-haves are SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and contractual data residency. We also need SOC2 and penetration test evidence.

01:50 Samir: We have SAML, support for customer KMS/HSM, and audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 report and pen-test summary. Private deployments can be configured with customer-controlled networking and KMS but require more setup time.
02:05 Tom: Ops question, how long to get Dedicated capacity online? We want to estimate timeline for POC that includes perf tests and a short integration window.

02:14 Jordan: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 2-4 weeks once contracts are done, provisioning included. Hosted benchmark we can start within 48 hours. Private—depends on network/legal, normally 6-10 weeks for full on-prem with HSM integration.

02:30 Miguel: For the POC success criteria, we care about: latency p95 < 200ms end-to-end, 99% uptime during our test window, accuracy drift less than 2% from our current baseline, and cost per inference target. Does that sound feasible to scope?
02:45 Samir: Yes that's reasonable. We'll need your sample traffic shape and token distribution to run realistic benchmarks. Also define the accuracy baseline and eval sets you want us to run.

03:05 Laura: We'll share a small dataset and some labeled cases. One question: how different are the latencies between hosted and dedicated? We've seen odd artifacts where hosted noisy multi-tenant behavior spikes latency.

03:20 Jordan: On hosted we provide performance profiles — for most workloads 95th latency is fine, but Dedicated removes the multi-tenant variance by reserving GPUs which tightens p95. For strict SLOs Dedicated or Private is usually chosen.
03:38 Priya: Also need to confirm data retention options and whether logs can be purged or exported to our SIEM. We can't have raw PII persist longer than 30 days in vendor systems.
03:49 Samir: We support configurable retention and can provide a pipeline to push logs into your SIEM. For Private deployments you can control retention fully on-prem.
04:05 Miguel: For benchmarking, we want p50/p95, cold start, warm cache, and end-to-end with our frontend included. Any recommended test harness?
04:18 Samir: We can run Redwood's benchmark harness against a hosted endpoint or a Dedicated pool. We'll need a tokenization profile — avg tokens/input and max tokens — and concurrency profile.
04:35 Miguel: Typical request is 120 tokens input, max response 60 tokens. Avg latency target needs to include network hop; our app sits in us-east-1 so region matters.

04:50 Jordan: We'll run benchmarks in us-east-1. For hosted we'll mirror your traffic for 24-72 hours to capture diurnal patterns; for Dedicated we can do a synthetic load to validate throughput and p95 once provisioned.
05:10 Laura: What about cost tradeoffs? Dedicated committed capacity makes sense if we need predictable spending but up-front commitments are a blocker for execs.

05:22 Jordan: Right — Dedicated trades commit for lower unit costs and latency predictability. Hosted is pay-as-you-go, easier to start, but unit cost is higher. Private adds integration and infra cost but is necessary for some regulated flows.
05:40 Tom: Is there a middle ground, like Dedicated in our VPC? We want network isolation but not full on-prem ops.
05:48 Samir: There's a VPC-hosted option for Dedicated where you get reserved capacity plus VPC peering/PrivateLink. It gives the network isolation you want with faster onboarding than pure on-prem.
06:02 Miguel: Ok, timeline-wise — if we decide Dedicated, we need a two-week POC window for benchmarking and then a pilot in prod. If Private, it'll push timelines by 6-8 weeks.

06:15 Jordan: That's accurate. For decision criteria: if compliance footnote requires on-prem KMS and no vendor egress, Private. If you need predictable latency/cost but can accept vendor-managed control plane, Dedicated. If speed-to-market and flexible scale matter, Hosted.
06:34 Priya: One more compliance ask — will Redwood sign subprocessor addendums and support customer-managed keys for hosted during the POC?

06:44 Samir: We can support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we have tenant encryption options and can discuss contractual KMS obligations — we'll surface the exact limitations in the security docs we send.
06:58 Laura: Sounds good. For measurable success, we'll define 3 KPIs: p95 latency < 200ms, model accuracy within 2% of baseline on eval set, and throughput sustaining 250 reqs/s for a 1-hour soak.
07:14 Jordan: Perfect. We'll draft that as the POC success criteria and include test cases. Anything else on the technical side?
07:22 Tom: For Dedicated, do we need any special network firewall rules? We usually lock down egress and only allow specific IP ranges.
07:31 Samir: We'll provide a network allowlist and can support PrivateLink. For Dedicated we provide static egress IPs for your firewall.
07:44 Miguel: Let's talk benchmarks specifics — we'd like to see both token cost and end-to-end latency. Can you measure tokenized cost per 1M tokens and also p50/p95 with client-side timing?
07:58 Jordan: Yes. Benchmarks will include per-token unit cost, GPU utilization, and p50/p95 E2E. We'll provide a spreadsheet results deck after the run.
08:12 Laura: On pricing, can you give a ballpark for Dedicated reserved capacity for our estimated load? We understand it's preliminary.
08:22 Jordan: I'll send SKU-based ballparks: monthly commit ranges and expected unit cost delta versus hosted. Expect 20-40% unit cost reduction at meaningful commit levels.
08:36 Priya: We'll also need legal to review DPA and subprocessor lists. Please attach those in the follow-up package.

08:46 Jordan: Will do. Recap of immediate next steps: Miguel will push sample traces and token distribution by 2026-05-19; Jordan will schedule hosted benchmark and send pricing by 2026-05-20; Samir will deliver SOC2 and security answers by 2026-05-21; we schedule private deep dive if needed.
09:05 Laura: One last quick thing — are there any known model compatibility caveats with our current quantized LLM experiments?

09:12 Samir: We had a few customers use quantized weights; our runtime supports popular quant formats. We'll validate your model/config during the POC. There can be small accuracy tradeoffs with aggressive quantization; we'll show that in the eval.
09:30 Miguel: Sounds good. Let's aim to have a decision point by 2026-05-26 after we see the benchmark results.
09:38 Jordan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the benchmark plan doc and calendar invites for the next calls. Thanks.
09:44 Laura: Thanks, bye.
End of transcript
